standard.title: Characteristic features by purpose
standard.description: identify the characteristic features used in imaginative, informative and persuasive texts to meet the purpose of the text
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify audience and purpose of texts through language features and images (AC9E3LY03). They have not yet identified the characteristic features of imaginative, informative and persuasive text types as distinct categories.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify the characteristic language features, visual features and structural features of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts and explain how each feature serves the text's purpose.

nodes.label: Imaginative text features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify characteristic features of imaginative texts and explain how each feature helps create imaginary worlds and engage readers.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two characteristic features of an imaginative text and explain how each contributes to its purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss a range of imaginative text features — descriptive language, figurative language, dialogue, narrative structure, character development — explaining how each feature creates the imaginary world and engages the reader.
wider: Compare imaginative text features across different forms — picture book, chapter book, graphic novel — and explain how the form affects which features predominate
Examine how First Nations Australian imaginative texts use features that reflect oral storytelling traditions and cultural knowledge
success_criteria: Can name two characteristic imaginative text features and link each to the text's purpose
Does not describe features as isolated techniques — connects each to the imaginary world or reader engagement

nodes.label: Informative text features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify characteristic features of informative texts and explain how each helps readers navigate, understand and use information.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two characteristic features of an informative text and explain how each helps the reader access information.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss a range of informative text features — headings, subheadings, captions, diagrams, bold text, topic sentences — explaining how each supports the reader's navigation and comprehension of information.
wider: Compare informative text features across digital and print formats — what features are shared and what differs, and why
Examine how informative texts use visual features (diagrams, charts, images) to complement or add to verbal information in a topic currently being studied
success_criteria: Can name two characteristic informative text features and explain how each helps the reader
Can distinguish between a visual feature (image, diagram) and a language feature (heading, topic sentence)

nodes.label: Persuasive text features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify characteristic features of persuasive texts and explain how each works to change the reader's views or actions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two characteristic features of a persuasive text and explain how each attempts to influence the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and discuss a range of persuasive text features — emotive language, rhetorical questions, evidence and statistics, repetition, call to action, inclusive pronouns — explaining how each is designed to position the reader to agree with the argument.
wider: Compare persuasive features across different persuasive text types — argument essay, advertisement, speech, opinion piece — and identify which features are shared and which are genre-specific
Examine how persuasive texts about topics related to Country, environment or community may use different persuasive strategies depending on the audience

response_modes.reason: Students often identify one or two persuasive features without understanding how they work together as a system. Multiple text types showing different combinations of features build a more complete understanding of persuasion.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of persuasive text types and features is wide, and the ability to identify how persuasion works is a critical literacy skill with genuine depth at this level.
success_criteria: Can name two persuasive features and explain how each attempts to influence the reader
Does not describe persuasive features as just 'convincing' — can explain the mechanism (e.g. emotive language makes readers feel something)
